name: CONGO
lead: Congo is a land of steamy rainforest in the heart of Africa — trees so thick sunlight barely reaches the ground. Gorillas, forest elephants, and thousands of birds live inside. The capital Brazzaville sits on the mighty Congo River, facing Kinshasa just 4 km away: two capitals closer to each other than any other pair on Earth.
geo: Congo's forests cover about 65% of the country — part of the world's second-largest tropical rainforest. The Congo Basin drains more water than any river except the Amazon.
The Congo River forms the eastern border and is so deep that fish have evolved completely blind. To the west, the Crystal Mountains rise before dropping to the Atlantic coast.
animals: Western lowland gorillas live deep in Odzala-Kokoua National Park — one of Africa's oldest protected areas. Family groups knuckle-walk through undergrowth, and visitors can sit just metres from a silverback.
Forest elephants are smaller and rounder-eared than savannah cousins. They create clearings called bais where dozens gather at mineral-rich mud pools. Over 400 bird species share these wild spaces.
culture: Congolese rumba — born from Bantu rhythms, Cuban music, and French ballroom — swept the world in the 1950s and is now UNESCO-recognised. Bands in Brazzaville still play late into the night.
Colourful pagne (wax-print cloth) is worn for weddings, church, and daily life. The Sape movement — dandies in flamboyant designer suits — turns Brazzaville's streets into a fashion show.
history: Bantu-speaking peoples settled the Congo Basin over 2,000 years ago. French explorer Pierre de Brazza signed a treaty with the Tio king in 1880, and the capital was named after him.
Congo became independent on 15 August 1960. Brazzaville made history in 1944 when de Gaulle held a landmark conference there that began reshaping France's ties with all its African territories.
wows: Brazzaville and Kinshasa are the only two capitals facing each other across a river — just 4 km apart.
The Congo River plunges over 220 m deep — enough to hide a 20-storey building completely underwater.
Congo's peatlands store ~30 billion tonnes of carbon — about 3 years of all global fossil-fuel emissions.
Oil makes up about 89% of Congo's exports, even though most of the country is pristine rainforest.
Odzala-Kokoua was first protected in 1935, making it one of Africa's oldest national parks.
The Congo–Ocean Railway took 13 gruelling years to build by hand through jungle, finishing in 1934.
Nearly 70% of Congolese live in cities — one of Africa's highest urban rates despite vast wilderness.

myths.fact: There are TWO Congos. Republic of the Congo (Brazzaville) is smaller and west of the river; DR Congo (Kinshasa) is much larger to the east.
Congo is one of Africa's most urbanised nations — about 70% live in cities with restaurants, music venues, and river promenades.
